name: Hwasong-17 intercontinental ballistic missile
overview_md:
The Hwasong-17 is North Korea's largest intercontinental ballistic missile — the so-called "monster missile" — and the centrepiece of Pyongyang's drive to hold the entire continental United States at risk with nuclear weapons. First revealed at a 2020 parade and flight-tested through 2022–2023, it is a road-mobile, liquid-fuelled, two-stage missile of exceptional size, carried on an eleven-axle transporter-erector-launcher.

Its estimated range — well over 13,000 km on a standard trajectory — is sufficient to reach anywhere in the United States, and its large throw-weight has fuelled assessments that it is designed to carry multiple warheads (MIRVs) or penetration aids to defeat U.S. missile defences. North Korea has tested it on lofted, near-vertical trajectories that demonstrate the range without overflying other countries.

For an analyst, the Hwasong-17 represents the maturation of North Korea's strategic deterrent and a direct complication for U.S. extended deterrence in the Indo-Pacific. Whether every claimed capability — re-entry vehicle survival, MIRV, accuracy — is fully proven remains debated, but the missile's existence changes the strategic equation: it underwrites Pyongyang's regime survival, stresses U.S. homeland missile defence, and shadows every alliance decision in Northeast Asia. It has since been joined by the solid-fuelled Hwasong-18, which is harder to detect and faster to launch.

variants_json.name: Hwasong-18 (related)
variants_json.key_changes: Solid-fuel ICBM — faster launch, harder to pre-empt

combat_history.event: Flight-tested on a lofted trajectory demonstrating intercontinental range.
combat_history.significance: Showed the ability to reach the continental United States.

combat_history.event: Paraded in large numbers, signalling production at scale.
combat_history.significance: Indicated a maturing, expanding ICBM force.

modernization.description: Shift toward solid-fuel ICBMs that launch faster and are harder to detect.

vulnerabilities.description: Liquid fuelling takes time and is detectable, creating a pre-launch window.
Re-entry vehicle survival and MIRV capability are not independently confirmed.
vulnerabilities.context: Claims rest on tests and parades.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Road-mobile, concealed and dispersed; lofted-trajectory tests demonstrate range.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Fielded; complemented by the solid-fuel Hwasong-18.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: China's road-mobile ICBM is more mature and solid-fuelled; the Hwasong-17 is North Korea's liquid-fuel equivalent.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The road-mobile ICBMs aimed at America.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The U.S. silo-based deterrent the Hwasong force is meant to deter and complicate.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: North Korea's bid for a credible US-range deterrent.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The KN-23 is a manoeuvring SRBM for the peninsula; the Hwasong-17 is the strategic intercontinental tier.

doctrine.role: Road-mobile intercontinental ballistic missile to hold the continental United States at nuclear risk.
doctrine.employment: Concealed mobile launchers; lofted-trajectory testing; possible MIRV/penetration aids against missile defence.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Maximum range and throw-weight to guarantee a US-range strategic deterrent.
doctrine.threat_context: Underwrites regime survival and complicates U.S. extended deterrence across Northeast Asia.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against China's DF-41, the U.S. Minuteman/Sentinel and North Korea's own KN-23.
